top_choice_rationale: P003 (Autor, Dorn and Hanson) offers the most identifiable co-authored unit and the most transparent, checkable identification on the slate. The local labour-market exposure design for import competition and technology shocks is a joint contribution that has been re-examined for a decade or more. The qualitative findings of slow adjustment and persistent local costs appear to have held up, though aggregate magnitude and persistence remain debated, and this rests on my recollection and is not verified here. I would limit the citation to the identified local-adjustment evidence so it does not claim the task framework, which is partly owed to Levy, Murnane, Acemoglu and Restrepo. Excluding Katz is a real cost. P002 (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) is second: its building blocks are separable and mature, but the eight-name credit pool and the unresolved theory-versus-estimation question make any trio contestable. P001 has the cleanest credit line but an uncredited Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum lineage and welfare claims that depend on functional form. P004 rests partly on observational cross-country identification and overlaps with the 2024 prize. No award is ranked last because every proposal is a defensible, mature achievement.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I disclose field proximity as a labour economist and AER editorial board member. My 2023 committee entry coincided with the Goldin prize, and Katz, a Goldin co-author, is on the B032 ballot but outside P003. None of the credited names in P003 is among my listed frequent co-authors.
